subject: North Ridge procurement: per-token tiers, PO line items, and vendor form workflow
messages:
From: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@nrhealth.org>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: North Ridge Procurement <procurement@nrhealth.org>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Preferred vendor form + pricing questions for Hosted API

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles. Procurement is working through the preferred vendor form and we hit a few snags on pricing and PO structure that we need clarified before we can push this to legal/finance. Key items below:

- The preferred vendor form asks for a "unit price"; your pricing is usage-based (per-token). Procurement insists on a PO line item with a price per unit. Can you provide guidance or a SKU-style mapping we can insert?
- They also need an example invoice that shows how overages are billed versus committed tiers. Can you provide a sample invoice with a monthly commit + overage reconciliation line?
- Our internal purchasing policy prefers fixed-line items on the PO (even for cloud consumption). Is Redwood able to accept a hybrid PO (estimated monthly commit line item + a true-up overage reconciliation)?

I attached the preferred vendor form the team started filling (NR_preferred_vendor_form_filled.pdf). If this needs to land on a different template, let me know.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement has a 2-week window for our vendor packet.

Best,
Samantha Clark
Head of Procurement, North Ridge Health
Samantha.Clark@nrhealth.org

[Attachment: NR_preferred_vendor_form_filled.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@nrhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred vendor form + pricing questions for Hosted API

Samantha — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) SKU / unit price mapping
We typically invoice usage as "tokens" at a per-token rate that depends on the commit tier. For procurement-friendly PO line items we can provide a SKU-like descriptor per tier. Example line items we can populate on your PO: 
  - REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-COMMIT-TIER1 — $0.00008/token (0–100M tokens/month)
  - REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-COMMIT-TIER2 — $0.00006/token (100M–500M tokens/month)
  - REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-OVR — $0.00010/token (overage)
These are illustrative; we can lock a unit price for a 12-month term if that helps procurement.

2) Sample invoice / reconciliation
Attaching a sample invoice that shows: committed allowance line, actual usage line, and net credit/charge for the month. See "sample-invoice-Q1-2027.pdf". This matches how we bill hosted customers today.

3) Hybrid PO approach
We support a hybrid PO: you can submit a fixed monthly/annual commit line (estimated tokens at tiered unit price) and then we reconcile overages monthly. For many customers procurement prefers a not-to-exceed value on the PO to satisfy internal controls — we can provide an annual maximum on the PO and then do monthly true-ups.

Next steps I propose: I attached a proposed PO template (redwood_proposed_po_template.xlsx) prefilled with SKU line items and a suggested annual cap. If that aligns, I can send a DocuSign-ready PO and our legal team will sign the vendor form.

Would procurement accept a 30-day true-up cycle and an annual price lock for committed tiers? Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call to walk the procurement team through the invoice and SKU mapping.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

[Attachments: redwood_proposed_po_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), sample-invoice-Q1-2027.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@nrhealth.org>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred vendor form + pricing questions for Hosted API

Samantha — Ben from Sales Ops here. Two quick operational notes to help procurement complete the vendor packet: 

- Billing codes: procurement can use the SKUs Marcus provided. In the PO template I added an extra column for your internal cost center and GL code so finance can map charges to the right ledger.
- Audit evidence: we can provide monthly token usage exports and an invoice CSV. If you need SOC2 or logging artifacts referenced on the vendor form, tell us which doc ID you want and I'll include it.

If procurement needs a single fixed number on the first PO submission, we can offer an "estimated monthly commit" line that equals the expected monthly spend (commit * unit price). We'll mark the PO with a note that charges beyond the committed estimate will be invoiced as overage with the agreed unit price and a monthly reconciliation.

Happy to update the XLSX with any GL or project codes you provide.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: North Ridge Procurement <procurement@nrhealth.org>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@nrhealth.org>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred vendor form + pricing questions for Hosted API

Marcus / Ben — thanks for the quick replies. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

- We cannot accept an "overage" with an open unit price on the PO. Procurement requires a price guarantee for the 12-month term. If overage pricing differs from the committed tier, that differential must be called out as a separate line item with a capped dollar value.
- The preferred vendor form expects a single vendor tax ID and a remittance address. Please provide your legal entity name, tax ID, and preferred remittance details so Accounts Payable can validate the vendor packet.
- We also need a DocuSign-ready vendor form — procurement will not sign PDFs that require separate countersignature. Do you have a DocuSign template or portal link?

We are willing to accept a hybrid invoice model but the PO must contain explicit fixed-line items for the term, including: committed tokens (line 1), guaranteed unit price (line 2), overage line with capped $ not-to-exceed (line 3). Once those fields exist in the PO, we can get this through our flow.

Samantha Clark
Head of Procurement, North Ridge Health
procurement@nrhealth.org

[Attachment referenced earlier: NR_preferred_vendor_form_filled.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: North Ridge Procurement <procurement@nrhealth.org>
Cc: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@nrhealth.org>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preferred vendor form + pricing questions for Hosted API

Samantha / Procurement team — understood and thanks for the clarity. Actions from Redwood: 

1) Legal / remittance details
  - Redwood Inference, Inc.
  - EIN: 12-3456789
  - Remit to: Redwood Inference, Inc., 101 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105

2) DocuSign template
  - I'll send a DocuSign-ready vendor form and a prefilled PO with explicit fixed-line items and a capped overage dollar amount. Link: https://docuSign.example.com/templates/redwood-nrh-po (internal link — will deliver via portal).

3) PO line items (example we will put on the template)
  - Line 1: REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-COMMIT — 120,000,000 tokens/month — unit price $0.00006/token — annual term
  - Line 2: REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-UNIT-PRICE-GUARANTEE — $0.00006/token (12-month locked unit price)
  - Line 3: REDWOOD-HOSTED-API-OVR-CAP — Overages billed at $0.00009/token, capped at $50,000/year

If that mapping meets procurement rules we will generate the DocuSign package tonight and share the link. Lauren — flagging for approval: this includes an introductory 8% volume discount on Tier1; legal has reviewed the vendor form and Finance is OK with the capped overage structure.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

[Attachments sent previously: redwood_proposed_po_template.xlsx, sample-invoice-Q1-2027.pdf]
